title: Assembly of compatible null-homotopies across a short exact sequence
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $0\to Z^\bullet\xrightarrow{i} I^\bullet\xrightarrow{\pi} B^\bullet\to0$ be a degreewise short exact sequence of cochain complexes, augmented by a compatible short exact sequence $0\to Z_0\to I_0\to B_0\to0$ such that the three augmented complexes are exact. Let $0\to J_Z^\bullet\xrightarrow{j} J_I^\bullet\xrightarrow{\rho} J_B^\bullet\to0$ be a degreewise short exact sequence of injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions], with compatible augmentations. Suppose a morphism of complexes $R_I:I^\bullet\to J_I^\bullet$ induces maps $R_Z:Z^\bullet\to J_Z^\bullet$ and $R_B:B^\bullet\to J_B^\bullet$ with $R_Ii=jR_Z$ and $\rho R_I=R_B\pi$, satisfies $R_I\epsilon_I=0$, and suppose $s_Z$ is a null-homotopy of $R_Z$ with $s_Z^0\epsilon_Z=0$. Then there are maps $s_I^q:I^q\to J_I^{q-1}$ and $s_B^q:B^q\to J_B^{q-1}$, with $s_I^0=s_B^0=0$, such that $R_I=d s_I+s_I d$, $R_B=d s_B+s_Bd$, $s_Ii=js_Z$, and $\rho s_I=s_B\pi$.

source.place: Tag 015I, compatibility of the boundary/cycle exact sequences; Weibel Homological Algebra, Lemma 5.7.10

proof.text: First choose, degree by degree, extensions $\widetilde{s}_Z^q:I^q\to J_Z^{q-1}$ of $s_Z^q$ across the monomorphisms $i^q$, using injectivity of the terms of $J_Z$. Since $J_Z^{q-1}$ is injective, the monomorphism $j^{q-1}$ has a retraction, so each short exact sequence $0\to J_Z^{q-1}\to J_I^{q-1}\to J_B^{q-1}\to0$ splits and $\rho^{q-1}$ has a section $\sigma^{q-1}$ with $\rho^{q-1}\sigma^{q-1}=1$ (the injectivity of $J_B^{q-1}$ is not what gives the section); independently choose the null-homotopy $s_B$ of $R_B$ with $s_B^0=0$ by the acyclic-to-injective null-homotopy result applied to the augmented exact complex $B$ (adjoin its augmentation object in degree $-1$, with the map $0$ there, a chain map because $R_B\epsilon_B=0$). The resolutions are indexed from degree $0$, so $J^{-1}=0$ and every map $I^0\to J^{-1}$ or $B^0\to J^{-1}$ is zero; in particular $s_B^0=0$ and $\widetilde{s}_Z^0=0$, hence $t^0=0$ below. The condition $R_I\epsilon_I=0$ implies $R_B\epsilon_B=0$, so this application has the required augmentation-zero condition.

source.place: Tag 015I, comparison construction for the boundary and cycle rows; Weibel Homological Algebra, Lemma 5.7.10

proof.text: Define $t^q=j\widetilde{s}_Z^q+\sigma^{q-1}s_B^q\pi^q$. Then $t i=j s_Z$ and $\rho t=s_B\pi$. Put $E=R_I-(d t+t d)$. The homotopy identity for $s_Z$ and the relation $R_Ii=jR_Z$ give $Ei=0$, while the homotopy identity for $s_B$ and $\rho R_I=R_B\pi$ give $\rho E=0$. Exactness therefore factors the defect uniquely as $E=jE'\pi$ for a chain map $E':B^\bullet\to J_Z^{\bullet}$; its augmentation composite is zero because $E\epsilon_I=0$ and $j$ is monic.

source.place: Tag 015I, compatibility of the boundary/cycle exact sequences

proof.text: Apply the same acyclic-to-bounded-below-injective null-homotopy result to the augmentation-zero map $E'$ (again adjoining the augmentation object in degree $-1$). It gives $k^q:B^q\to J_Z^{q-1}$ with $k^0=0$ and $E'=d k+k d$. Define $s_I=t+j k\pi$ and retain $s_B$. Then $R_I=d s_I+s_I d$, because $E=jE'\pi$, while $s_Ii=js_Z$ and $\rho s_I=s_B\pi$ because $\pi i=0$ and $\rho j=0$.

source.place: Tag 015I, compatibility of the boundary/cycle exact sequences; Weibel Homological Algebra, Lemma 5.7.10

proof.text: The chosen homotopies vanish in degree zero, so $s_I^0=s_B^0=0$; the displayed identities give all required conclusions.
